## Load packages

`pacman` loads the required packages and installs any that are missing. `here::i_am()` places
this notebook in the repository, so paths resolve from the repository root. `pROC` and
`enrichVolcano` (the user's own package, not on CRAN) are called with `::` for one function each.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tidyr, purrr, stringr, ggplot2, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/05_set_classification/a_script/05_set_classification.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

Three inputs: the set catalogue from `00_build_gene_sets`, the singscore matrix from
`04_run_singscore` (one row per set, one column per sample) and the sample targets stored with
the protein estimates. The singscore matrix travels as rds, not through a workbook, because a
round trip through xlsx breaks the exact rank ties the tests below depend on. Reading
`proteins.rds` loads limma, which defines its stored class, and R says so in the output.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "05_set_classification")
set_catalog <- read_excel(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"),
  "set_catalog"
)
set_score <- readRDS(here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "04_run_singscore", "c_data", "set_scores.rds"))
targets <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))$targets
dim(set_score)
head(targets[c("sample_id", "participant", "leg", "treatment", "timepoint")], 6)
```

## Select sets

Only sets the catalogue marks as `qualifies` are tested. `values` holds their scores in catalogue
order, and `collection_sizes` counts sets per collection; that count is the denominator for the
chance comparison further down.

```{r select-sets}
catalog <- set_catalog |>
  filter(qualifies) |>
  select(set_id, database, pathway, measured_size)
values <- set_score[catalog$set_id, ]
collection_sizes <- count(catalog, database)
collection_sizes
```

## Pair the samples

Every comparison here is paired, so each sample needs its partner. `by_timepoint` spreads the
targets to one row per leg, with the T1 and T2 sample IDs side by side. `legs` keeps legs sampled
at both time points. Treatment comes from the targets, never the leg letter: leg assignment was
counterbalanced.

```{r pair-legs}
by_timepoint <- targets |>
  mutate(leg_id = paste(participant, leg, sep = "_")) |>
  select(leg_id, participant, leg, treatment, timepoint, sample_id) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = sample_id)
legs <- drop_na(by_timepoint, T1, T2) |> arrange(participant, treatment)
head(legs, 4)
```

`pair_by_treatment()` takes a leg table and the name of the column that identifies each leg, and
returns one row per participant holding both legs, BFR and HLRT, in that column. Participants
missing either leg are dropped.

```{r pair-participants}
pair_by_treatment <- function(data, column) {
  data |>
    select(participant, treatment, value = all_of(column)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = value) |>
    drop_na(BFR, HLRT)
}
baseline <- pair_by_treatment(by_timepoint, "T1")
post <- pair_by_treatment(by_timepoint, "T2")
delta_pairs <- pair_by_treatment(legs, "leg_id")
c(legs = nrow(legs), baseline = nrow(baseline), post = nrow(post), change = nrow(delta_pairs))
```

The change in each set's score per leg is T2 minus T1. Its columns are named by leg, so the BFR
and HLRT legs of a participant can be picked out with `delta_pairs`.

```{r change-scores}
delta <- values[, legs$T2] - values[, legs$T1]
colnames(delta) <- legs$leg_id
```

## Define the tasks

Each task holds a score matrix and two paired column sets: `positive` and `negative`, matched
position by position. Pre against post compares the two time points within each arm. The three
BFR against HLRT tasks compare the two legs of each participant at baseline, after training and
in change. `favours` is the group an AUC above 0.5 points to, so the figures can state direction.

The baseline comparison is legs before any training, so it shows what the method returns when
nothing is there. It is reported in the chance table but not drawn.

```{r tasks}
arm <- split(legs, legs$treatment)
tasks <- list(
  pre_vs_post_BFR = list(
    values = values, positive = arm$BFR$T2, negative = arm$BFR$T1,
    label = "Pre to post, BFR", favours = "post", unit = "legs"
  ),
  pre_vs_post_HLRT = list(
    values = values, positive = arm$HLRT$T2, negative = arm$HLRT$T1,
    label = "Pre to post, HLRT", favours = "post", unit = "legs"
  ),
  baseline_BFR_vs_HLRT = list(
    values = values, positive = baseline$BFR, negative = baseline$HLRT,
    label = "Baseline BFR vs HLRT", favours = "BFR", unit = "participants"
  ),
  post_BFR_vs_HLRT = list(
    values = values, positive = post$BFR, negative = post$HLRT,
    label = "Post BFR vs HLRT", favours = "BFR", unit = "participants"
  ),
  delta_BFR_vs_HLRT = list(
    values = delta, positive = delta_pairs$BFR, negative = delta_pairs$HLRT,
    label = "Change, BFR vs HLRT", favours = "BFR", unit = "participants"
  )
)
drawn_tasks <- setdiff(names(tasks), "baseline_BFR_vs_HLRT")
tibble(
  task = names(tasks), label = map_chr(tasks, "label"),
  pairs = map_int(tasks, function(spec) length(spec$positive)), favours = map_chr(tasks, "favours")
)
```

## Score each set

Two numbers per set and task. The AUC (area under the ROC curve) is the probability that a
randomly chosen positive sample scores higher than a randomly chosen negative one: 0.5 is no
separation, 1 perfect separation upward, 0 perfect separation downward. It is computed from ranks
and ignores the pairing. The p-value comes from the paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, which ranks
the within-pair differences and asks whether they centre on zero, so it uses the pairing.

`fit_roc()` takes one set's scores and a task, and returns the ROC fit. `paired_test()` takes a
task and returns one row per set with its AUC and paired p. Ties among the differences make
`wilcox.test()` warn that it cannot give an exact p; it falls back to the normal approximation,
and the warning is suppressed.

```{r paired-tests}
# pROC::roc() auto-orients: a true AUC of 0.194 comes back 0.806. direction = "<" pins it.
fit_roc <- function(values, spec) {
  pROC::roc(
    controls = values[spec$negative], cases = values[spec$positive],
    direction = "<", quiet = TRUE
  )
}
paired_test <- function(spec) {
  tibble(
    auc = apply(spec$values, 1, function(row) as.numeric(pROC::auc(fit_roc(row, spec)))),
    p_paired = apply(spec$values, 1, function(row) {
      suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(row[spec$positive], row[spec$negative], paired = TRUE)$p.value)
    })
  )
}
```

Run every task, stack the results and attach each set's collection and name. BH adjustment runs
within each task and collection, never pooled across them.

```{r set-auc}
# The argument is `spec`, not `task`: tibble() builds a `task` column first, and a later
# `task$label` in the same call would read that column instead of the argument.
set_auc <- imap(tasks, function(spec, name) {
  tibble(
    task = name, task_label = spec$label, set_id = rownames(spec$values),
    n_pairs = length(spec$positive), paired_test(spec)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  left_join(select(catalog, set_id, database, pathway), by = "set_id") |>
  mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p_paired, "BH"), .by = c(task, database))
head(arrange(set_auc, p_paired), 6)
```

## Check results

One row per task: every set tested once, the AUC range and any missing p-value.

```{r check}
set_auc |>
  summarise(
    sets = n(), auc_min = min(auc), auc_max = max(auc), missing_p = sum(is.na(p_paired)),
    .by = task
  )
```

## Compare with chance

With thousands of sets, some reach p < 0.05 by luck alone. The chance expectation is 5% of the sets
tested: the number of nominal hits a collection returns when no set truly separates the groups.
The ratio of observed nominal hits to that count reads 1 at chance. Each collection gets its own
denominator, so a 41-set collection is not read against a 1,366-set one, and BH runs inside the
same split for the same reason.

```{r chance}
chance_expectation <- set_auc |>
  transmute(
    analysis = "classification", comparison = task_label, database, n_pairs, p = p_paired, fdr
  ) |>
  summarise(
    features = n(), nominal = sum(p < 0.05), expected = round(n() * 0.05, 1),
    ratio = round(nominal / expected, 2), fdr_sig = sum(fdr < 0.05),
    .by = c(analysis, comparison, database, n_pairs)
  )
head(chance_expectation, 6)
```

## Draw figures

The figure helpers below are shared line for line with `06_set_association`. `figure_theme` is
the common look. `caption_text()` takes a figure title, the caption text and the page position,
and returns the wrapped caption. `paginate()` takes rows with a `panel` factor and a function that
draws one page, and returns a list of plots, twelve panels to a page. It builds each page from
that page's rows, because a paginating facet would build every panel for every page.
`chance_page()` draws the chance ratios as bars. `write_pdf()` writes a list of plots to one A4
PDF in `b_reports/`.

```{r figure-helpers}
figure_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 6.8, lineheight = 1.2, margin = margin(3, 3, 4, 3)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(4, "mm"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, lineheight = 1.2),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    legend.position = "top"
  )
caption_text <- function(title, text, page = 1, n_pages = 1) {
  pages <- if (n_pages > 1) sprintf(" (page %d of %d)", page, n_pages) else ""
  str_wrap(sprintf("%s%s. %s", title, pages, text), 115)
}
paginate <- function(data, draw, title, text, scales = "fixed") {
  pages <- split(data, (as.integer(data$panel) - 1) %/% 12)
  imap(unname(pages), function(page, i) {
    draw(droplevels(page)) +
      facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 3, nrow = 4, scales = scales) +
      labs(caption = caption_text(title, text, i, length(pages))) +
      figure_theme
  })
}
chance_page <- function(data, y, facet, title, text) {
  ggplot(data, aes(ratio, .data[[y]], fill = ratio > 1)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
    geom_col(width = 0.65) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sprintf("%d of %d", nominal, features)),
      hjust = -0.12, size = 2.5, colour = "grey25"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[facet]]), ncol = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#B2182B", `FALSE` = "grey72"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22))) +
    labs(
      x = "observed nominal hits / chance expectation", y = NULL,
      caption = caption_text(title, text)
    ) +
    figure_theme +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
write_pdf <- function(pages, name) {
  pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", name), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
  walk(pages, print)
  invisible(dev.off())
}
```

`chance_line()` takes a collection and returns the caption sentence giving its chance count.
`set_label()` turns a collection and pathway name into a wrapped panel title.

```{r label-helpers}
chance_line <- function(db) {
  n <- collection_sizes$n[collection_sizes$database == db]
  sprintf("Nominal p, uncorrected: chance alone returns %.1f of the %d %s sets.", n * 0.05, n, db)
}
set_label <- function(database, pathway) {
  str_wrap(paste0(database, ": ", enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway, width = 1000)), 40)
}
```

`roc_figure()` takes a task, its S-number and a collection, and returns the ROC pages for every
set in that collection reaching nominal p on that task, smallest p first, or an empty list when
there are none. An ROC curve plots the true positive rate against the false positive rate as the
score threshold moves; the area under it is the AUC.

```{r roc-figure}
roc_figure <- function(task_name, number, db) {
  spec <- tasks[[task_name]]
  hits <- set_auc |>
    filter(task == task_name, database == db, p_paired < 0.05) |>
    arrange(p_paired)
  if (nrow(hits) == 0) {
    return(list())
  }
  curves <- pmap(hits, function(set_id, database, pathway, auc, p_paired, fdr, ...) {
    coordinates <- pROC::coords(fit_roc(spec$values[set_id, ], spec), "all")
    tibble(
      fpr = 1 - coordinates$specificity, tpr = coordinates$sensitivity,
      # An AUC below 0.5 separates the groups the other way, so it is coloured by direction.
      direction = if_else(auc >= 0.5, "higher", "lower"),
      panel = sprintf(
        "%s\nAUC %.2f   p %s   q %s",
        set_label(database, pathway), auc, signif(p_paired, 2), signif(fdr, 2)
      )
    )
  }) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel))) |>
    arrange(panel, fpr, tpr)
  paginate(curves, function(page) {
    ggplot(page, aes(fpr, tpr, colour = direction, fill = direction)) +
      geom_abline(linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey60") +
      geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = tpr), alpha = 0.16, colour = NA) +
      geom_step(linewidth = 0.7, direction = "hv") +
      scale_colour_manual(
        values = c(higher = "#B2182B", lower = "#2166AC"), aesthetics = c("colour", "fill"),
        guide = "none"
      ) +
      coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
      scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
      labs(x = "1 - specificity", y = "sensitivity")
  }, sprintf("S%d Figure", number), paste(
    paste0(spec$label, ", ", db, "."),
    sprintf(
      "ROC curves for all %d %s sets whose singscore separates the groups at nominal p, across %d",
      nrow(hits), db, length(spec$positive)
    ),
    sprintf("paired %s, smallest p first. AUC has its direction fixed: red", spec$unit),
    sprintf("separates higher in %s, blue lower.", spec$favours),
    "Shading is area under the curve, dashed line chance. p from the paired Wilcoxon",
    "signed-rank test, q from BH within collection and task.", chance_line(db),
    "Data: set_auc sheet of 05_set_classification.xlsx."
  ))
}
```

One PDF per collection, so each can be read on its own. The four drawn tasks are S12 to S15 in
the order of `drawn_tasks`; S16 is the chance page across all five tasks.

```{r write-figures}
walk(unique(catalog$database), function(db) {
  write_pdf(
    list_flatten(imap(drawn_tasks, function(task_name, i) roc_figure(task_name, 11 + i, db))),
    paste0("05_classification_", db, ".pdf")
  )
})
write_pdf(list(chance_page(
  mutate(chance_expectation, comparison = factor(comparison, map_chr(tasks, "label"))),
  "database", "comparison", "S16 Figure", paste(
    "Nominal hits relative to chance, by collection. Paired Wilcoxon per set across",
    nrow(collection_sizes), "collections, uncorrected p. Bar length is observed nominal hits",
    "divided by the count that collection returns under the null; red clears 1, grey does not.",
    "Labels give observed of tested. Data: chance_expectation sheet of 05_set_classification.xlsx."
  )
)), "05_chance_by_collection.pdf")
```

## Summary

Nominal hits as a multiple of chance, by task and collection, then the sets surviving BH in each
task. Training moves the pre against post ratios well above 1; the BFR against HLRT tasks,
baseline included, sit near or below it.

```{r summary}
chance_expectation |>
  select(comparison, database, ratio) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = database, values_from = ratio)
summarise(chance_expectation, fdr_sig = sum(fdr_sig), .by = comparison)
```

## Save results

`05_set_classification.xlsx` opens with an `overview` sheet, then `chance_expectation` (nominal
hits against chance per task and collection), `set_auc` (AUC, paired p and BH q per set and task,
smallest p first) and `set_catalog` (every tested set).

```{r write}
sheets <- list(
  chance_expectation = chance_expectation,
  set_auc = arrange(set_auc, p_paired),
  set_catalog = catalog
)
overview <- data.frame(
  sheet = names(sheets), rows = map_int(sheets, nrow), columns = map_int(sheets, ncol),
  description = c(
    "Nominal hits against chance, per collection. Read this first.",
    "How well each set separates each task. AUC from ranks, p from paired test.",
    "Every tested set with its collection and measured size."
  )
)
write_xlsx(
  c(list(overview = overview), sheets),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "05_set_classification.xlsx")
)
```
